newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria aluminium smelter delayed further.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria aluminium smelter delayed further.

text.p: The start-up of Nigeria's aluminium smelter, scheduled for this month, has been put back further, the official Business Times newspaper reported on Monday.
It said the project at Ikot Abasi in the southeast was not yet fully completed and no new date was projected.
The plant was originally scheduled to come on stream last October, and in January power and steel minister Bashir Dalhatu announced that it would be commissioned in March.
March came and went without any official explanation of the delay.
No officials were available on Monday to comment on the Business Times report.
According to Dalhatu, the plant had been completed and the postponement was to allow for dredging of the Imo River so that big ships would be able to move finished products from the plant.

The 180,000 tonnes a year project, begun in 1990, is a joint venture between Nigeria, which has 70 percent, and Ferrostaal AG of Germany and Reynolds International of the U.S., which share the rest of the equity.
The two foreign technical partners have formed a subsidiary firm called EBE and Reynolds to manage the plant for 10 years.
A pipeline to supply natural gas, the main raw material, was completed last year by Nigeria Gas Company, a subsidiary of state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp.
The World Bank has been critical of the project, saying it was ill-conceived and expensive.
But Nigeria says the plant would earn hard currency from exports and reduce imports of ingots and billets for the large local aluminium products industry.
